survey: A beach ball resting on rippled sand, seen from slightly above with dunes rising behind it. The outline is a true circle (E1 ratio 0.97, 0.7% off), as a sphere should be. The purple valve cap sits at the top-front pole and is tilted toward the camera. It is drawn as an ellipse roughly 0.6 as tall as it is wide. That matches its position: it sits about 0.58 of the radius above the ball's centre, which gives a predicted squash of about 0.59. The panels fan out from the cap as meridians: red, white, blue, white, green and white. The blue/white seam that passes through the centre of view is almost straight (near 88°). The seams to either side bow outward more the further they are from centre. Panels near the front look widest and narrow as they wrap toward the silhouette, and the green panel disappears over the top-right edge. The ball's lower edge meets the sand from the same slightly high viewpoint that shows the cap from above, and its shadow falls on the ground to the right. Everything agrees on one camera.
